Note API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This is the per-method reference for pluss::Note — one page per method, in the same handwritten, compiled-and-verified style as the rest of the PlussQit object references. For building a Note, see the separate Note Factory API Reference; everything on this page assumes a Note already exists.

What Note Is¶

Note is PlussQit’s low-level text value. A Note is a shape (up to 3-D) of text cells — UTF-8 by default, or raw bytes — and its methods transform those cells in a vectorized, shape-preserving way, the same way Series transforms numbers and Timeline transforms instants.

Reach for Note when the data are strings, tokens, lines, snippets, prompts, document fragments, or LaTeX, and the work is cleanup, matching, rewriting, splitting, tokenization, regex extraction, or text-oriented natural-language preprocessing.

How The Methods Are Shaped¶

Most Note methods preserve shape and act cell by cell: a rank-1 Note of three cells maps to a rank-1 Note of three cells. A few families break that mould:

  • Predicates — contains, starts_with, ends_with, the is_* character-property checks (is_alpha, is_digit, is_blank, …), and regex_match / regex_search return a flat std::vector<std::uint8_t> of 0/1, one entry per cell in row-major order.

  • Measurements — lengths_bytes, lengths_chars, lengths_graphemes, and count_substring return a flat std::vector<std::int64_t>, one entry per cell.

  • Tokenizers — split, split_lines, split_whitespace, tokenize_words, and regex_findall, and the diff / align family (diff_words, diff_lines, diff_chars, align_tokens, align_sentences) return a TokenBatch: one flat token Note (batch.tokens()) plus an offsets() vector (std::vector<std::int64_t>, length numel + 1) that marks where each input cell’s run of tokens begins and ends in the flat stream. Row r’s tokens are tokens()[offsets()[r] .. offsets()[r+1]).

  • Set-similarity comparisons — the intersect_*, jaccard_*, and overlap_* methods each take a second Note and compare cell against matching cell (equal numel, or a scalar broadcast). intersect_* (intersect_tokens, …) return a TokenBatch of the shared tokens; jaccard_* (jaccard_tokens, …) and overlap_* (overlap_tokens, …) return a shape-preserving Note whose cells are similarity scores formatted as strings in [0, 1].

  • Shape & layout — reshape, flatten, squeeze, unsqueeze, transpose, permute, and contiguous change the rank or axis order of a Note without touching a single cell string.

  • Cell access & ownership — at and at_indices borrow one cell as a std::string_view; cell, cell_at, and owned return a TextRef that keeps the packed arena alive; host materializes rank-aware owning standard-library strings.

  • Borrowed structural projections — scalar borrows the sole cell regardless of rank; vector flattens every rank; matrix preserves rank two and promotes lower ranks; tensor3 requires exact rank three; sizes_view borrows the extents without allocating.

Running The Examples¶

Every example is a runnable fragment (assume #include <pluss/pluss.h> and #include <iostream>), and every ### Output block is copied verbatim from a permanent compiled reference executable. The cell-access family is verified by examples/CodeN/note_access_reference_demo.cpp, with its exact transcript in docs/sphinx/_verified/note_access_reference_output.txt; broader transformation examples remain in examples/CodeN/note_method_reference_demo.cpp. Structural projection examples are verified by examples/CodeN/note_projection_reference_demo.cpp, with its exact transcript in docs/sphinx/_verified/note_projection_reference_output.txt. Collection reduction and ordering examples are verified by examples/CodeN/note_collection_reference_demo.cpp, with its exact transcript in docs/sphinx/_verified/note_collection_reference_output.txt.

To print a Note, any of these render byte-identical text, and the pages rotate through them:

std::cout << pluss::note::print(n) << "\n";  // print(n) -> std::string
std::cout << n << "\n";                       // operator<< (default options)
pluss::note::print(std::cout, n) << "\n";     // print(os, n) -> the stream

The non-Note results are printed plainly:

// contains / lengths_bytes: a flat vector, one entry per cell
const auto mask = n.contains("x");
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

// a TokenBatch: the flat token Note, then the offsets
const auto batch = n.split(",");
std::cout << pluss::note::print(batch.tokens()) << "\n";
std::cout << "offsets: [";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < batch.offsets().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << batch.offsets()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Examples that show a rejection call the method inside a try block and print the first line of pluss::Error::what() (the message); what() also appends a Triggered at: location line, which the output blocks omit.

Coverage¶

This reference documents the methods users reach for first:

  • Metadata and rank — defined, dim, size, sizes, numel, empty, is_scalar, is_vector, is_matrix, and is_tensor3.

  • Case — lower, upper, casefold, title, capitalize, swapcase.

  • Boundary trimming — strip, lstrip, rstrip.

  • Whitespace & layout — collapse_whitespace, collapse_spaces, collapse_newlines, collapse_repeats, collapse_punct, dedent, indent, remove_control_chars, to_ascii.

  • Unicode normalization — to_nfc, to_nfd, to_nfkc, to_nfkd, strip_accents, strip_bom, strip_zero_width, normalize_quotes, normalize_dashes, normalize_ellipsis.

  • Character-class filters — remove_punctuation, remove_symbols, remove_digits, remove_letters, remove_emojis, keep_alnum, keep_alpha, keep_digits, keep_ascii, keep_printable.

  • Rewriting — replace, replace_first, replace_last, replace_n, regex_replace, remove, remove_all, remove_prefix, remove_suffix, ensure_prefix, ensure_suffix, surround, quote, unquote.

  • Inspection — contains, contains_any_alpha, contains_any_digit, starts_with, ends_with, count_substring, regex_match, regex_search, is_alpha, is_alnum, is_digit, is_lower, is_upper, is_title, is_whitespace, is_blank, is_ascii, is_utf8_valid, is_bytes, lengths_bytes, lengths_chars, lengths_graphemes.

  • Tokenizers — split, split_lines, split_whitespace, tokenize_words, regex_findall.

  • Diff & align — diff_words, diff_lines, diff_chars, align_tokens, align_sentences.

  • Set similarity — intersect_tokens, intersect_terms, intersect_acronyms, intersect_citations, intersect_math_symbols; jaccard_* and overlap_* for the same five token-set kinds.

  • Targeted masking — nlp_mask_pii, nlp_remove_urls.

  • TeX — tex_escape, tex_to_text.

  • Transport encodings — base64_encode/base64_decode, hex_encode/hex_decode, url_encode/url_decode.

  • Escaping — html_escape/html_unescape, json_escape, tex_escape/tex_to_text.

  • Encoding & transcoding — to_utf8_strict, to_utf8_lossy, from_latin1/to_latin1_lossy, from_windows1252/to_windows1252_lossy — convert between a bytes-mode payload and UTF-8 text.

  • Transliteration & phonetics — transliterate_ascii (and its synonym transliterate_latin), transliterate_greek, transliterate_cyrillic; phonetic_soundex, phonetic_metaphone.

  • Shape & layout — reshape, flatten, squeeze, unsqueeze (synonym expand_dims), transpose, permute, contiguous. These are metadata-only: the cell strings are untouched, only the rank and axis order change.

  • Selection & slicing — select (one slab along an axis, that axis dropped), narrow (a contiguous range along an axis, rank kept), take (gather cells by an index list, rank-1 result).

  • Collection reduction & ordering — join reduces all text cells to a scalar Note, join_flat extracts one owning standard string, sort orders lanes, unique returns sorted distinct values or slices, and deduplicate keeps their first-seen order.

The rest of the Note surface — broader cleanup, NLP extraction, and the remaining structural operations (repeat, repeat_interleave) — is documented method by method in later passes.
